q: What is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature?
f: Gallium melts in your hand at about 30°C, but mercury is liquid at room temperature.

q: What is the capital of Australia?
f: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

q: Which planet has the most known moons?
f: Saturn passed 270 known moons in 2025, far ahead of Jupiter.

q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
f: The Berlin Wall opened on 9 November 1989.

q: Which organ produces insulin?
f: Insulin is made by beta cells in the pancreas.

q: What is the chemical symbol for tungsten?
f: W comes from 'wolfram', tungsten's other name.

q: Which country has the most time zones (incl. territories)?
f: Thanks to its overseas territories, France spans 12 time zones.

q: Who painted 'The Starry Night'?
f: Van Gogh painted it in 1889 from an asylum in Saint-Rémy, France.

q: What is the hottest planet in our solar system?
f: Venus's thick CO2 atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter than Mercury.

q: What is the smallest prime number?
f: 2 is the only even prime number. 1 is not prime.

q: What is the fastest bird in a dive?
f: Peregrine falcons can exceed 300 km/h when diving.

q: What is the longest mountain range on land?
f: The Andes run about 7,000 km along South America.

q: What gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
f: Nitrogen is about 78% of the air; oxygen about 21%.

q: Who was the first person to reach the South Pole?
f: Amundsen's Norwegian team got there on 14 December 1911.

q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
f: Two atria and two ventricles.

q: Which language has the most native speakers?
f: Mandarin has the most native speakers; English has the most total speakers.

q: What is the closest star to Earth after the Sun?
f: Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light-years away.

q: Which river flows through the most countries?
f: The Danube flows through or borders 10 countries.

q: What is the hardest natural substance?
f: Diamond scores 10, the top, on the Mohs hardness scale.

q: Which empire built Machu Picchu?
f: The Inca built it in the 15th century high in the Andes of Peru.

q: How many sides does a dodecagon have?
f: 'Dodeca' comes from the Greek for twelve.

q: Which mammal can truly fly?
f: Bats are the only mammals capable of powered flight; others glide.

q: What is the smallest country in Africa by area?
f: The Seychelles islands cover only about 455 km².

q: What is the speed of light, roughly?
f: Light travels about 299,792 km every second.

q: Who wrote 'One Hundred Years of Solitude'?
f: The Colombian author won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.

q: Which planet spins on its side?
f: Uranus is tilted about 98°, so it rolls around the Sun.

q: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
f: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969.

q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
f: An adult's skin covers about 2 square metres.

q: Which country has the most islands?
f: Sweden is estimated to have over 260,000 islands.

q: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
f: About three-quarters of normal matter is hydrogen.

q: How many keys does a standard piano have?
f: 52 white keys and 36 black keys.

q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
f: Two pump blood to the gills, one to the rest of the body.

q: What is the deepest lake in the world?
f: Lake Baikal in Russia is about 1,640 m deep.

q: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
f: She won in Physics (1903) and again in Chemistry (1911).

q: What is the value of 0! (zero factorial)?
f: By definition 0! = 1, which keeps many formulas working.

q: What is the largest volcano in the solar system?
f: Olympus Mons on Mars rises about 22 km high.

q: What is the pH of pure water at 25°C?
f: pH 7 is neutral: neither acidic nor basic.

q: Which desert is the driest non-polar desert?
f: Some weather stations in Chile's Atacama have never recorded rain.

q: What does 'HTTP' stand for?
f: HTTP was created by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN around 1990.

q: Which ancient wonder still stands today?
f: It is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

q: Which blood type is the universal donor for red cells?
f: O negative red cells can be given to almost anyone in an emergency.

q: What is the largest living species of lizard?
f: Komodo dragons can grow to about 3 metres long.

q: What is the capital of Canada?
f: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857.

q: Who proposed the theory of general relativity?
f: Einstein published general relativity in 1915.

q: How long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth?
f: Sunlight travels about 150 million km in roughly 8 minutes 20 seconds.

q: In which country was 'Don Quixote' written?
f: Miguel de Cervantes published it in two parts, in 1605 and 1615.

q: What is the square root of 144?
f: 12 × 12 = 144, also called a gross.

q: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
f: At about 5,895 m it is Africa's highest mountain.

q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
f: He proposed it at CERN in 1989.

q: What particle has a negative charge?
f: Electrons orbit the nucleus, which holds protons and neutrons.

q: Which animal has the largest eyes?
f: A colossal squid's eye can be about 27 cm across.

q: Which is the largest country in South America?
f: Brazil covers almost half of South America.

q: How many players are on a football (soccer) team on the field?
f: Each side fields 10 outfield players plus a goalkeeper.

q: What is at the centre of our Milky Way galaxy?
f: It's called Sagittarius A*, about 4 million times the Sun's mass.

q: Where is the smallest bone in the human body?
f: The stapes in the middle ear is only about 3 mm long.

q: Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the USA?
f: It was dedicated in New York Harbor in 1886.

q: Which vitamin does sunlight help your skin make?
f: UVB light lets the skin produce vitamin D.

q: What is the next prime number after 7?
f: 8, 9 and 10 can all be divided by smaller numbers.

q: In which year was the first iPhone released?
f: Steve Jobs unveiled it in January 2007; it went on sale that June.

q: What do you call a baby kangaroo?
f: A newborn joey is about the size of a jellybean.

q: Which ocean is the largest?
f: The Pacific is bigger than all of Earth's land combined.

q: Which civilization invented paper?
f: Cai Lun is credited with improving papermaking around 105 CE.

q: What is absolute zero in Celsius?
f: -459.67 is absolute zero in Fahrenheit, not Celsius.

q: Which was the first artificial satellite?
f: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957.

q: Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?
f: It was published in 1813.

q: Which country is home to the city of Timbuktu?
f: Timbuktu was a great centre of learning in the 15th–16th centuries.

q: What is the normal resting heart rate range for adults?
f: Very fit athletes can be lower than 60 beats per minute.

q: Which bird lays the largest eggs?
f: An ostrich egg can weigh about 1.4 kg.

q: Which planet is known for having diamond rain inside it?
f: Scientists think the pressure inside Neptune and Uranus can turn carbon into diamonds.

q: Who was the first emperor of Rome?
f: Julius Caesar was a dictator; his heir Augustus became the first emperor in 27 BCE.

q: What is the highest waterfall in the world?
f: Angel Falls in Venezuela drops about 979 m.

q: How many degrees are in the angles of a triangle?
f: This is true for any flat triangle.

q: What does 'CPU' stand for?
f: The CPU carries out a program's instructions.

q: Which planet has the shortest year?
f: Mercury goes around the Sun in just 88 Earth days.

q: What is a group of crows called?
f: A 'parliament' is a group of owls.

q: Which country has the longest coastline?
f: Canada's coastline is over 200,000 km long.

q: What does DNA stand for?
f: Its double-helix shape was described in 1953.

q: In which city was the Titanic built?
f: It was built at the Harland and Wolff shipyard.

q: Which part of the eye controls how much light gets in?
f: The iris widens or narrows the pupil.

q: What is the capital of Turkey?
f: Ankara became the capital in 1923.

q: In which country were the first modern Olympic Games held?
f: Athens hosted them in 1896.

q: What is the name of the largest moon in the solar system?
f: Jupiter's Ganymede is even bigger than the planet Mercury.

q: Which element has the atomic number 1?
f: A hydrogen atom has just one proton.

q: Which animal sleeps standing up and can't vomit?
f: A strong valve stops horses from vomiting.

q: Which country has the most pyramids?
f: Sudan has around 200 or more ancient Nubian pyramids, more than Egypt.

q: What is 15% of 200?
Who wrote the 'Theory of Evolution by Natural Selection'?
f: 'On the Origin of Species' was published in 1859.

q: Which company created the Android operating system before Google bought it?
f: Google bought Android Inc. in 2005.

q: How many planets in our solar system have rings?
f: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune all have rings.

q: Which line divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
f: The Equator is about 40,075 km long.

q: What force keeps planets in orbit around the Sun?
f: Gravity and the planets' sideways speed together create orbits.
